title: a contended write waits five seconds on a timeout nobody chose, set by a dependency default that is invisible to every reader of our source
body:
**A CONTENDED WRITE BLOCKS FOR FIVE SECONDS AND THEN REFUSES, AND THE FIVE SECONDS IS A CONSTANT NOBODY CHOSE, NOTHING DOCUMENTS, AND NO READER OF OUR SOURCE CAN SEE.**

**MEASURED 2026-08-30 by cc, CONSTRUCTED rather than reasoned** -- a fresh fixture project under its own `$HOME`, with a second process holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on the store while the shipped CLI writes. Controls driven before and after:

```
CONTROL, no lock     st new   rc=0  0.01s
WRITE, lock held     st new   rc=1  5.22s   "could not update the runtime store /
                                             sqlite: database is locked ... remedy:
                                             the change was not made. Do NOT delete the store"
READ, lock held      st list  rc=0  0.01s   readers never block
AFTER RELEASE        st new   rc=0  0.01s   store intact, thread created normally
```

## The safety half is fine and is recorded here so nobody re-opens it

**A second writer is refused cleanly with an accurate message and a remedy, and nothing is corrupted.** A whole sync is ONE transaction -- `commit_mutation` has exactly one caller and takes every changed thread, issue, section, removal and creation as slices in a single `Mutation` -- so two engines cannot half-apply a sync. **This issue is NOT about corruption.**

## The defect is the invisible constant

**`rusqlite` 0.32.1 hardcodes `sqlite3_busy_timeout(db, 5000)` in `inner_connection.rs:119` on every open.** Nothing in this workspace sets it, nothing documents it, and it does not appear in any file a maintainer would read.

**IT PRODUCED A CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER FROM A SOURCE READ, WHICH IS HOW IT WAS FOUND.** cc read `store.rs`, observed correctly that no `busy_timeout` is set anywhere in our code, and concluded that a second writer fails immediately -- **wrong by five seconds, and only the constructed case corrected it.** A dependency's default is invisible to source reading by construction, so this class cannot be found by review; it is found by driving the contended path or not at all.

**THE HARM IS TO WHOEVER TUNES A DEADLINE NEXT.** `AC-08.3` sets a bounded round-trip deadline for daemon liveness and `AC-08.11` requires the daemon answer on the accept path ahead of per-request work. **A maintainer sizing either against our source will not see a five-second block sitting in the write path**, and the two numbers interact -- which is exactly why `AC-08.11` puts the probe answer ahead of request handling, arrived at independently and now doubly justified.

## And the user-visible cost, which is poor rather than unsafe

A user meeting the contended path waits **five seconds** and is then refused. The refusal is correct, the message is accurate and it names a remedy; **the pause is unexplained and looks like a hang.** In this five-node shared checkout the contended path is not hypothetical.

## What closes this

**Choose the value deliberately and say so where a reader will find it** -- set `busy_timeout` explicitly in `store.rs` even if the chosen value is 5000, so the constant is ours and visible rather than a dependency's default nobody selected. **Setting it to the same number is not a no-op**: it converts an invisible inherited behaviour into a recorded decision, which is the whole defect. If a shorter wait plus an immediate refusal is better for an interactive CLI, that is a separate judgement this issue does not pre-empt -- but it cannot be made at all while the number is unseeable.
